title: Checkpoint staging: intermittent GCS timeouts and partial shard downloads
content:
Notes-to-self / incident breadcrumbs (staging cluster)

Context:
- Trying to stage a 350GB model checkpoint (128 shards) into staging GPU pool for smoke tests. Failures intermittent: some nodes finish, others error mid-download, causing partial/torn tar parts.
- Symptoms: python loader sees truncated shard (EOFError / tarfile.ReadError) or checksum mismatch on final sha256. Sometimes gsutil reports 503.

Timeline & commands tried:
1) Initial manual replica pull (from staging pod):
   $ python tools/stream_fetch.py --source gs://rdw-checkpoints/model-v2 --shard 59 --out /tmp/shard-59.tar
   -> [ERR] Traceback (most recent calls): EOFError: Unexpected end of data (read 42 bytes)
   Check: sizes differ from manifest (expected 2.8GB, got 1.1GB)

2) Re-run with curl range to validate resumability:
   $ curl -I "https://storage.googleapis.com/rdw-checkpoints/model-v2/shard-59.tar"
   HTTP/2 200
   Accept-Ranges: bytes

   $ curl -r 0-1073741824 -o part1 ".../shard-59.tar"
   -> succeeded. Fetching later ranges occasionally returned 503s

3) gsutil copy with retries:
   $ gsutil -o 'GSUtil:parallel_process_count=1' -m cp gs://rdw-checkpoints/model-v2/shard-59.tar /tmp/
   -> cp failed after ~2GB with: "AccessDeniedException" (unlikely) or transient 503
   Tried: gsutil -o 'Boto:https_validate_certificates=False' -D cp ... (debug) -> same pattern

4) gcloud auth and service account sanity check
   - Confirmed service account has storage.objects.get/list on bucket (iam audit shows OK)
   - No apparent quota exhaustion; bucket logs show sporadic 500/503 around 2025-11-04 18:20-18:32 UTC (matching failures)

Hypotheses:
- Partial object corruption at upload time (less likely since other shards okay).
- GCS regional egress/intermittent backend flakiness causing stream resets -> tar stream truncated leading loader errors.
- Too many parallel range requests from our downloader hitting per-object proxy limits -> backend rate-limits/returns 503.
- Metadata/manifest inconsistency: manifest listed the uncompressed size but object is compressed (weird), causing early EOF when we naively stream expecting raw tar size.

What I tried to reduce flakiness:
- Reduce parallelism: set MAX_PARALLEL=2 in downloader; broke into sequential range requests. Improved success rate from ~70% to ~92% on staging.
- Exponential backoff with jitter: implemented (base=1s, max=30s) for 503/429/500; helped but still occasional failures.
- Switch to signed URL per object (short-lived) and curl -> no improvement (still 503s occasionally).
- Use resumable download (gsutil or google cloud storage API) which writes to tmp+compose. This works more often but still fails mid-upload when writing to disk due to node OOM in one of the staging nodes (investigate node memory).
- Verified object CRC32C/MD5 in bucket metadata for random good shards: match manifest. For failed shards, metadata present and correct according to bucket index (leans away from corruption).

New idea: range request pacing + preflight HEAD and conditional GETs
- Before streaming, HEAD (or GET with Range: bytes=0-0) to ensure object is served from stable backend. If 200 OK + Accept-Ranges header then proceed.
- Throttle concurrent active range requests for the same object to 1 and add 300ms inter-request gap. Early experiments show a reduction in 503s.

Repro commands to debug from a staging pod (notes):
- Check kernel dmesg for OOMs: dmesg | tail -n 200
- Monitor NIC errors: ethtool -S eth0 | egrep 'err|drop'
- Curl with verbose and capture http2 frames: curl -v --http2 "https://storage.googleapis.com/.../shard-59.tar" -o /tmp/x ; tail /tmp/x ; (watch for TLS reset)
- Small python snippet to stream and log Content-Range headers and retries:
   import requests, time
   url = 'https://storage.googleapis.com/rdw-checkpoints/model-v2/shard-59.tar'
   r = requests.head(url)
   print(r.headers.get('Accept-Ranges'))
   def get_range(s,e):
       for i in range(6):
           rr = requests.get(url, headers={'Range': f'bytes={s}-{e}'}, stream=True, timeout=30)
           if rr.status_code in (200,206):
               return rr
           time.sleep((2**i)+0.1)
       raise RuntimeError('range failed')

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is this limited to the staging GCS bucket location? Check by copying object to a different regional bucket and re-trying staging pulls.
- Could our egress NAT gateway / VPC-SC or proxy be rate-limiting large, many-range flows? Check VPC logs and proxy (squid/nginx) metrics.
- Add more logging to downloader: record response headers (server, x-goog-generation, x-retry-after) and time-to-first-byte.
- Try alternative transfer path: gsutil -o 'GSUtil:resumable_threshold=10M' cp (force resumable) vs single-shot range streaming.
- If repeated failures are >5% for full staging run, fall back to replicating a pre-staged disk image (one-time rsync) instead of per-shard downloads.

Notes on rollback safety:
- Loader already does partial-shard detection (size mismatch + sha check). Ensure we do not mark model as staged until all shards verified. Add a "staging-atomic" marker object when all shards pass; current implementation only sets marker at end but if process crashed mid-mark, we might have stale marker — add pre-check for marker creation timestamp and uploader identity.

Immediate next steps (today):
- Push small change to downloader: throttle per-object range concurrency to 1, add exponential jitter, log headers. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/weights-downloader/pull/213 (wip).
- Run full staging 3x with these settings and collect failure rate + bucket logs + pod dmesg.
- If failures persist, escalate to infra to check GCS egress path and NAT gateways.

Random thoughts (notes-to-self):
- Could we ship shards first to GCE local SSD snapshot and image the node? Too heavyweight for quick dev but useful for full-scale predictable CI.
- Consider checksum-on-read approach: stream into temp and verify before atomically moving into model dir. We already do this, but double-check race conditions when two pulls race to same temp file.

End of notes.

Unresolved: still see intermittent 503s in bucket logs for the time windows where failures happen. Need infra to correlate pod IP -> NAT -> GCS backend."
